name: Aidoc
description: Aidoc is privately held and has no ticker. Review its funding rounds, its investors, and the points to confirm before buying or selling.
ledes: Aidoc is a privately held clinical AI company. Its shares are not listed on an exchange and have no quoted market price, and the company has not disclosed the valuations at which it has raised capital. Its most recent financing, a $150 million Series E round, was announced on April 29, 2026.

Founded in 2016 and based in New York, Aidoc develops AI software that reviews medical images for urgent conditions and alerts the clinicians responsible for treatment. Existing shares change hands in privately negotiated transactions and remain subject to the company's transfer restrictions.

table_note: Aidoc has not disclosed a valuation for any of these rounds. The July 2025 growth round of $150 million included a $40 million revolving credit facility.
round_notes: The Series E was led by the growth equity business of Goldman Sachs Alternatives. With its announcement, Aidoc said its software was deployed in nearly 2,000 hospitals; that figure is the company's own.

A round valuation reflects the terms of the preferred stock issued in that round. Most shares sold by employees are common stock, which carries fewer rights and typically trades at a discount to the preferred price.
investors: Goldman Sachs Alternatives led the Series E, with participation from General Catalyst, SoftBank Investment Advisors and NVentures, Nvidia's venture capital arm. General Catalyst and Square Peg led the July 2025 growth round, in which the health systems Mercy, Hartford HealthCare, WellSpan Health and Sutter Health also invested; TCV and Alpha Intelligence Capital co-led the Series D, and General Catalyst led the Series C. Other investors include CDIB Capital, TLV Partners and Magma.
spv_sentence: No special purpose vehicles naming Aidoc appear in SEC Form D filings.
sources: Sources: Aidoc's announcements of its Series E, Series D and Series C; reports by Healthcare Dive (July 2025), HIT Consultant (July 2025), Calcalist (April 2026) and Globes (April 2026); and SEC Form D filings.
